chapter_title: The Interpretation of Happiness, Wisdom and Power; what they signify.
chapter_note: The oldest teaching layer is a four-fold descending iteration mapping happiness, wisdom, and power to cosmic beings at four levels: (1) the Father/land of light, (2) the sun ship, (3) the moon ship, (4) the elements. Each iteration follows the same triadic structure (happiness=sovereign being, wisdom=cognitive/generative being, power=the gods/angels at that level). This is pure cosmos→cosmos mapping. An editor extended this to a fifth level (the holy church, ¶9) by mimicking the pattern syntax — detected by bridge connective 'Now, moreover' and institutional vocabulary. The chapter's editorial fatigue score confirms significant institutional drift in the second half (+4.77). The summary in ¶10 integrates the editorial extension ('five churches') and closes with a beatitude. Paragraphs 1-4 are frame/setup with the topic question in ¶2 being substantive.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Pure formulaic opening. '[Once aga]in the enlightener speaks to his disciples' is the stereotyped frame formula. 'assembly of the church' adds institutional coloring.

paragraphs.core_text: [What] are these thr[ee things] that in the world are called 'happine[ss', 'wisdom]', and 'power'?
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed 'People boa[s]t of th[em ... ] the happiness of the world [ ... ] in the world it has a [ ... ] of the world shall pass by.' — editorial rhetoric contrasting worldly transience with cosmic truth. This is homiletic framing, not cosmos→cosmos mapping.
paragraphs.temporal_note: The substantive question defines the teaching topic (three cosmic principles: happiness, wisdom, power) and generates the four-fold iteration that follows. The rhetoric about worldly boasting and passing away is editorial setup voice. Heavy lacunae obscure some content.

Heavily damaged. Surviving content is entirely rhetorical/editorial: 'People boast of them. They praise...' continues the worldly contrast rhetoric; 'as I have told you' is self-referential back-reference. No cosmological mapping survives. Functions as editorial bridge between the topic question and the systematic teaching.

Entirely first-person pedagogical framing: 'I will teach you of another happiness... listen that I may reveal to you.' The concept of 'another' (true/cosmic) happiness/wisdom/power is implicit in the teaching structure but here it is expressed in the teacher's instructional voice, not in systematic mapping. The topic was already established in ¶2.

paragraphs.core_text: [The happin]ess of the glorious one is the Father, the God of [truth, who] is established in the great land of [light]. ⟨p.24⟩ His glorious wis[d]om is his Great Spirit that [ ... ] below, which flows through all his aeons, and t[h]ey float therein. His great power is all the gods, the rich ones and the angels who were summoned from him as they [ ... ] t]hey that are called aeons [ ... ]
paragraphs.temporal_note: FIRST ITERATION — Land of Light / the Father. Happiness=the Father in the land of light; Wisdom=the Great Spirit flowing through the aeons; Power=the gods, rich ones, and angels summoned from him. Pure cosmos→cosmos mapping. Both sides internal: sovereign being → cosmic attribute → emanated beings. The triadic structure (sovereign/cognitive/collective) repeats at each level.

paragraphs.core_text: [ ... ] which is called] the sun [ ... the ship of] living fire, [ ... the Third Amba]ssador, the second greatne[ss ... The] glorious [happiness] is the [Living] Spirit, [ ... , the wisdom] is the Mother of Lif[e ... and great power] is [all] the gods, [the] rich o]nes and the angels who are within the ship.
paragraphs.temporal_note: SECOND ITERATION — The Sun / Ship of Living Fire. Heavily damaged but structure clear: Happiness=Living Spirit; Wisdom=Mother of Life; Power=gods, rich ones, angels within the ship. The Third Ambassador is identified with 'the second greatness.' Same triadic pattern descends one cosmic level.

paragraphs.core_text: Again, [h]appiness, wisdom and power exist in the s[hip of liv]ing waters [ ... ] the happiness [ ... ] the Mind of the Father. Also, wisdom [is the Vir]gi]n of [Li]ght. And the power that is [i]n the ship is [all] the go[ds], the [ri]ch ones and the angels who are established i[n it].
paragraphs.temporal_note: THIRD ITERATION — The Moon / Ship of Living Waters. Happiness=Mind of the Father; Wisdom=Virgin of Light; Power=gods, rich ones, angels established in the ship. 'Again' is an iteration marker integral to the teaching structure. The triadic pattern continues its descent.

paragraphs.core_text: Again, these three exist in the elements: happiness, wis[d]o]m and power. The happiness is [the Pillar of Glory], the Perfect Man. Wisdom is the [five sons of the] Living Spirit; and great powe[r is ... the fi]ve sons of the First Man [ ... who are encl]osed and compounded in the totality, that [ ... ] while he supports the totality.
paragraphs.temporal_note: FOURTH ITERATION — The Elements / Mixed World. Happiness=Pillar of Glory/Perfect Man; Wisdom=five sons of Living Spirit; Power=five sons of First Man. This is the lowest cosmic level: beings 'enclosed and compounded in the totality.' The substrate vocabulary 'enclosed and compounded' describes the mixture condition. 'Supports the totality' may refer to the Pillar of Glory's cosmological function.

EDITORIAL SEAM — confirmed. 'Now, moreover' is the bridge connective that extends the four-fold cosmic iteration to a fifth level: the holy church. The pattern syntax is mimicked exactly (happiness=X, wisdom=Y, power=Z) but Mapping Side B now reaches into the editor's institutional world: 'Apostle of Light who has been sent', 'leaders and teachers who travel in the holy church proclaiming wisdom and truth', 'elect, virgins, continent, catechumens.' Every identification is institutional. The preceding four iterations map cosmos→cosmos; this one maps cosmos→church hierarchy. The entire paragraph is one editorial act.

Devotional closure. 'Blessed, therefore, is every one who will know them' is the standard beatitude formula. The summary 'five happinesses, five wisdoms, five powers in the five churches' integrates the editorial extension (¶9) into the count — 'five' rather than 'four' reflects the editor's addition. 'Five churches' applies institutional framing to all cosmic levels. The summary + beatitude form a single editorial closure act. Note: it is possible the original teaching had a fifth cosmic level that the editor replaced with the church, but this cannot be reconstructed from surviving text.
